h1:
Uttaradit Mookata
8 BBQ Grill Buffets for Dinner
intro: Once the sun drops and the air cools off, people in Uttaradit start meeting up at the local mookata joints — because dinner over a sizzling grill, with everyone talking for hours, is basically the town's evening ritual. From cheap all-you-can-eat buffets near the university to Japanese-style grill spots in town, we picked 8 places locals actually go, with straight talk on prices and which part of town they're in.
chips: 🔥 Buffets from a couple hundred baht

blocks.html: Mookata in Uttaradit isn't just one thing. There are all-you-can-eat buffets at friendly prices, à la carte spots where you order sets, and newer Japanese-style grill places in town. The main cluster of well-known shops sits in front of Uttaradit Rajabhat University, where several joints line up along one street — so you can walk down and pick based on your budget and the mood that night.

blocks.text: 8 Mookata and Grill Spots Uttaradit Locals Actually Go To

blocks.html: Ordered from the most-packed value buffets down to the grill spots with a slightly nicer atmosphere. The prices listed are rough figures from recent reviews and can shift with promos and the time you go, so it's worth checking the shop's page before you head out.

items.name: Fah Sai Mookata Buffet (Uttaradit Branch)
items.blurb: The first place locals in Uttaradit think of for buffet. The draw is more seafood to grill than the average spot — shrimp, shellfish, marinated pork, beef, and fresh veggies, all you can take. The room is big with lots of tables, so it works well for a large group or bringing the whole family.

items.name: Lang Suan Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: Right in front of Uttaradit Rajabhat University, this is the buffet students and nearby workers go to regularly. Ingredients are fresh — pork, beef, chicken, and plenty of vegetables — with a punchy dipping sauce and easygoing prices. A solid pick for a dinner where you just want to eat your fill without overthinking it.

items.name: Sahai Ka Kung Buffet
items.blurb: A buffet that rolls mookata, grill, jim jum hot pot, and butter-grill all into one place. The selling point is fresh shrimp to grill, so it's good for seafood lovers, and the more people you bring the better the deal — there's a per-head discount for groups of five or more.

items.name: Charoen Phung Mookata
items.blurb: A newer spot in front of Uttaradit Rajabhat University, down the soi near MOMO Shake / Yui Cha. It sells sea-themed sets where you pay for what you eat — eat more, pay more; eat less, pay less — starting at 299 THB per set. Good if you don't want a full buffet but still want grilled seafood.

items.name: Pan Pan Shabu & Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: A quieter find outside town that not everyone has caught on to yet, just before Ban Na Yang School in Phichai district. The draw is a 189 THB buffet (drinks not included) plus open-field views and a relaxed feel. Drive out a little and you get both cheap eats and breezy seating — bring up the map for directions.

items.name: Ruay Mit Mookata (Soi Rewadi 60)
items.blurb: An à la carte spot that stays open late, with mookata, pork hot pot, and snacks to share. Good for people who want to sit and talk for a long time or come by after work — the vibe is laid-back, no rush, since it closes later than most.
items.price: By the plate, à la carte

items.name: Waku Waku at TT Garden
items.blurb: Japanese-style grill and shabu buffet, one of the first of its kind in Uttaradit. The room looks nicer than your typical mookata place, so it suits a day when you want to celebrate or take someone special. There's a 2-hour seating limit including drinks, and the price climbs to match the meat quality and the atmosphere.

items.name: Buf Co (Uttaradit Branch)
items.blurb: A grilled-beef buffet in the center of town serving wagyu-style fattened beef, pork, and seafood. It's clean and comfortable, suited to people who want grilled beef as the main event rather than homestyle mookata. There are opening promos worth checking on their page.

blocks.title: Local tip
blocks.html: Most buffets get packed between 18:30–20:00, so if you don't want to wait for a table, go before 6pm or call ahead to book and you'll have an easier time. Many places also charge less per head for bigger groups, so rounding up some friends makes it cheaper.

blocks.text: How to Pick the Right Spot

items: Budget, eat all you want — aim for buffets near Rajabhat University like Lang Suan, or Pan Pan in Phichai district; prices start at a couple hundred THB.
Love grilled seafood — Fah Sai, Sahai Ka Kung, and Charoen Phung have more shrimp and shellfish to grill than the average spot.
Want a nice atmosphere for a special day — Waku Waku for Japanese-style, or Buf Co for grilled beef; both are more comfortable to sit in.
Coming late, staying long — Ruay Mit on Soi Rewadi 60 is open until 11pm, good after work.

blocks.text: Get the Most Out of Mookata in Uttaradit

blocks.html: Mookata here is about being easygoing — not fancy, but you get that dinner-with-friends feel. What makes the meal more fun is coming with a bunch of people, since you get to share lots of dishes and many places charge less per head. If you're driving, the shops near the university and in town usually have easy parking.

items: Start by grilling vegetables and thin slices of meat first, then move on to seafood — the grill gets more fragrant as you go.
Top up the broth around the rim of the grill often; it picks up the sweetness from whatever you're grilling and pairs well with the grilled food.
Many buffets fine you if you leave a lot behind, so take just enough and go back for more — it works out better.
Bring cash. Some smaller shops still don't take transfers or cards.

faq.q: Which mookata spot in Uttaradit is the best value?
faq.a: For all-you-can-eat value, Pan Pan in Phichai district starts at 189 THB (drinks not included), which is a good price. In town, Lang Suan in front of Rajabhat University also starts at a couple hundred THB, and many places charge less per head when you come as a group.

faq.q: Where should I go if I want grilled seafood?
faq.a: Fah Sai Mookata has plenty of seafood to grill, all you can take. Sahai Ka Kung stands out for fresh shrimp, while Charoen Phung Mookata in front of Rajabhat University does a sea-themed menu sold by the set, starting at 299 THB.

faq.q: What time do mookata shops in Uttaradit open?
faq.a: Most open in the evening, around 16:00–17:00, and run until 9 or 10pm. A place like Ruay Mit on Soi Rewadi 60 stays open until 11pm, good for people coming after work.

faq.q: Are there any grill spots with a nicer atmosphere?
faq.a: Yes — Waku Waku at TT Garden is a Japanese-style grill-and-shabu spot with a 2-hour seating limit, around 329–429 THB, and Buf Co in the town center focuses on grilled beef. Both are more comfortable to sit in than a typical mookata place, so they suit a special day.

faq.q: Which area are most of the shops in?
faq.a: The main cluster of well-known shops is in front of Uttaradit Rajabhat University, where several line up along one street so you can walk and choose. Some cheaper buffets are outside town around Phichai district, a short drive out.
